summary.text: 九 is a whole-graph pictograph interpreted as an arm associated with the elbow. Early inscriptions use it for both a body part read as elbow or wrist and the numeral nine. A proposed sound-based borrowing may account for the numeral, but the pictured object’s spoken name is unknown, so the sound link remains unverified.

formation.text: 九 is analyzed as a single pictograph of an arm associated with the elbow. A distinct historical account describes a bent shape reaching its end; a dragon-or-serpent interpretation is also recorded, but neither alternative establishes the graph’s origin.

components.text: The graph is treated as one whole picture, interpreted as an arm associated with the elbow; its exact referent is uncertain. It is not analyzed as a compound of smaller elements.

history.text: 九 appears in oracle-bone inscriptions and in Shang–Zhou bronze and Warring States writing. These broad comparisons do not trace a dated, step-by-step development into later scripts.
The selected oracle-bone and bronze-script illustrations are modern redraws assigned to different script styles, not a dated sequence. The bronze form has no specific period assigned.

uncertainties.text: The arm-and-elbow interpretation has a competing wrist reading. The depicted object and its original spoken name remain uncertain.

One account proposes that the graph was reused for nine because the depicted object’s old name sounded similar to the word for nine. Since that name is unknown, the proposed sound match cannot be verified.

senses.text: A cited oracle-bone passage uses 九 for a body part read as elbow or wrist, consistent with the interpretation that the graph is an early form associated with 肘.
Oracle-bone examples use 九 for nine, including a count of oxen and a month date. These examples do not establish whether numeral use preceded or followed the body-part use.
Later transmitted-text examples use nine to express a large or extreme quantity; the timing and path of this extension are unclear.
九 is reported as a loan spelling for 鳩. This is a separate use of the graph, not evidence that the meaning “nine” developed into “dove”; the reason for reuse is not given.
九 is the current numeral nine.

developments.text: Later uses extend the numeral nine to express a large or extreme quantity, though the chronology is unspecified.

limitations.text: The cited examples support both body-part and numeral uses but do not establish their relative chronology or why the graph came to write nine. One account proposes sound-based borrowing, but the depicted object's spoken name is unknown, so the proposed sound match cannot be verified.
The cited oracle-bone inscriptions and later transmitted-text examples are not precisely dated here.

overview.text: 九 means nine and is interpreted as a whole picture of an arm. A proposed borrowing links it to nine through sound, but the pictured object’s name is unknown, so the match remains unverified.

components.text: This analysis treats 九 as one whole picture, possibly an arm associated with the elbow; its exact referent is uncertain.
